parsed_response.reasoning: The diff changes deleteEvent's fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (previously a single object) to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, no calendar can have `externalId === externalCalendarId` (falsy), so the find always fails and calendarId becomes undefined, whereas the old code returned the destination calendar's externalId. Same dead-predicate issue in updateEvent (line with `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)`). This is a real regression introduced by this diff: deletes/updates on bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId will no longer target the destination calendar.

judged_text: deleteEvent's fallback branch has the same dead predicate — `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` where externalCalendarId is guaranteed falsy by the enclosing ternary — so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId. Cancelling a Google booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now issues the delete with calendarId undefined (or the 'primary' default), so the event on the actual destination calendar is never removed and stays orphaned on the host's Google Calendar after the Cal.com booking is gone.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the fallback calendar id like:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
(and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`). In the `:` branch, `externalCalendarId` is necessarily falsy/undefined, so the `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` predicate is effectively `cal.externalId === undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid externalId. From the diff, call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking`) pass `externalCalendarId` from booking references and that value can be null/absent, making this fallback path relevant. This can lead to issuing updates/deletes against an undefined calendarId / defaulting to `primary` rather than the actual destination calendar, leaving orphaned events.
